conviction_note: Two of three months of Q3 sales are public (July +15.5%, August +16.6% daily) and imply revenue of about $2.47bn against a stale $2.43bn bar. August headcount growth slowed to +0.6% y/y from +1.9% at June-end, which supports SG&A leverage and an EPS of about $0.34-0.35. Against that, the August mix (contract customers +19% vs non-contract +11%, heavy manufacturing +21.8%, indirect fasteners +11.7%) and management's statement that price-cost will not close in 2H point to a gross margin near 44.3-44.5%, down 80-100bp y/y. That is the line this stock was sold on in Q2 (-2.78%) and Q1 (-6.85%). The findings net to about zero (-0.2). The scaled number, p_up 47 x abs 4.8 = -0.29, leans slightly negative only because the last three prints were sold, the skew pays for downside and the EPS bar is disputed between $0.33 and $0.34.
bar: Revenue $2.43bn and EPS $0.33 from Benzinga consensus (snapshot around mid-August, before the August sales release; https://www.benzinga.com/quote/FAST/earnings-forecasts). AAII also gives $0.33 from 14 analysts (https://www.aaii.com/investingideas/article/514050-what-you-need-to-know-about-fastenal-companys-q3-earnings), but FN2 shows a Q3 EPS estimate of $0.34 (https://fn2.ai/earnings/fast/2026-q2/analysts/all). The revenue bar has one stale source and the EPS bar is disputed by a cent, so every finding is capped small. print_vs_bar_pct is measured against the $2.43bn revenue bar; against a bar refreshed after August (plausibly about $2.46bn) it would be about +0.4%.
positioning_check: Short interest was 34.6m shares, 3.03% of float, 4.6 days to cover at the 2026-09-30 settlement (published 2026-10-09), down 2.9% from the prior report (https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NASDAQ/FAST/short-interest/). That is not crowded, so there is no squeeze mechanism against a negative. Baseline: 25-delta skew +4.14 vol points (downside paid), put/call OI 2.13, event-implied move 5.68% against a median historical reaction of 2.78%. Spot is 2.85% below the 52-week high after a +2.99% 20-day run-up.

findings.finding: Fastenal's own July and August 2026 sales releases give daily sales of $37.538m (+15.5%, 22 days, $825.8m) and $38.670m (+16.6%, 21 days, $812.1m). With September at the 2021-25 average sequential pattern, which ISM's September PMI of 54.5 (new orders 55.3) does not contradict, Q3 revenue comes to about $2.46-2.48bn, +15-16% y/y, against the mid-August $2.43bn consensus.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 beat on sales ($2.387bn, +14.7%) with in-line EPS and the stock fell 2.78%. The last three prints were all sold (-2.78, -6.85, -2.56) despite double-digit sales growth.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. The monthly releases are public and sell-side updates its sales models from them; only September is new. If it were fully priced, the consensus would read about $2.46-2.47bn rather than the $2.43bn snapshot, and I could not find a post-August consensus to check. The stock sits near its 52-week high, which fits the strength being known.
findings.independence: ISM September 2026 Manufacturing PMI 54.5 and New Orders 55.3, the ninth month of expansion (https://www.ismworld.org/supply-management-news-and-reports/reports/ism-pmi-reports/pmi/september/). Grainger raised its 2026 outlook on 2026-08-04 on broad acceleration (https://distributionstrategy.com/2026/08/grainger-extends-growth-streak-as-industrial-digital-businesses-drive-double-digit-gains/).

findings.finding: The August release shows total FTE up only 0.6% y/y (selling FTE -0.5%) against sales up 16.6%, compared with FTE +1.9% (selling +0.9%) at the end of Q2, when SG&A already levered 80bp. That supports Q3 SG&A of about 23.5% of sales against 24.6% a year ago, an operating margin of about 21%, and EPS of about $0.34-0.35 against a bar of $0.33-0.34.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In Q2 2026, 80bp of SG&A leverage held operating margin flat at 21.0% and EPS came in line at $0.33. The market looked through the leverage and sold the GM decline (-2.78%).
findings.why_not_priced: Headcount sits in a table at the bottom of a monthly release that previews and the wire do not quote. If it were priced, EPS estimates would have moved to $0.35 with sales; the visible bars are $0.33-0.34. On the Q2 call management also cited bonuses and fuel as costing a couple of points of incremental margin, which partly offsets.
findings.independence: Q2 2026 10-Q and release: employee-related SG&A leverage of 70bp and FTE +1.9% at June-end (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000815556/000081555626000037/ex_99106302026earningsrele.htm). Same company, different document. The August headcount table shares a document with finding 1 but is a different line (opex, not revenue).

findings.finding: Q3 gross margin is likely to land at about 44.3-44.5%, down 80-100bp y/y from 45.3% and a larger y/y decline than Q2's 75bp. On the Q2 call management guided a normal 10-20bp sequential seasonal drop and said the 40bp price-cost gap is not expected to close in 2H. The August mix adds pressure: contract customers +19% vs non-contract +11%, heavy manufacturing +21.8%, and higher-margin indirect fasteners only +11.7%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: This is the line the stock trades on. Q2 2026 GM fell 75bp and the stock fell 2.78%; Q1 2026 GM trailed estimates on cost headwinds and the stock fell 6.85% (https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-04-13/fastenal-s-gross-margin-trails-estimates-on-cost-headwinds).
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. The skew (+4.1, downside paid) and put/call OI of 2.13 agree with this, and management guided the seasonal drop. What may not be priced is the mix effect from accounts growing faster in August, which a model built on the seasonal guide would not include. If it were fully priced, the stock would not be within 3% of its 52-week high.
findings.independence: The August mix data comes from a different document, the August sales release (https://s25.q4cdn.com/185498701/files/doc_financials/2026/Q3/August/08-2026-sales-numbers-v3-1.pdf). The Q2 10-Q attributes GM pressure to price/cost, customer mix, transport and rebates (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000815556/000081555626000041/fast-20260630.htm). Note that this finding lands largely inside what management already guided.

findings.finding: The Q2 10-Q says Fastenal filed IEEPA refund claims for the imports where it was importer of record but had recorded no receivable at 2026-06-30, and that it 'may recognize additional benefits in future periods'. Grainger booked $43m (+90bp of GM) of such refunds in Q2. A Q3 recognition would be a small GM help, but Fastenal says its direct exposure is limited.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Fastenal has no history on this line. Across the repo, tariff-refund recognitions moved stocks in the direction of guidance, not of the refund.
findings.why_not_priced: No estimate bakes in an unrecorded gain contingency. Because Fastenal is not the importer of record for most products, the dollars are likely small and a one-off below the run rate, so it is sized at a fraction.
findings.independence: Grainger Q2 2026 release, $43m of IEEPA refunds in COGS (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000277135/000027713526000076/gww8kex991q22026.htm).

findings.finding: The ISM September 2026 Prices index jumped 6.8 points to 77.9. Accelerating input-cost inflation makes it harder for Fastenal's account-by-account pricing to close the 40bp price-cost gap, which is a risk to the Q4 gross margin commentary, though it is also a tailwind to sales pricing.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In Q1 2026 management said tariffs were rising faster than it could raise prices, and the stock fell 6.85%.
findings.why_not_priced: This is a macro-to-company proxy and the ISM is public. What may not be priced is the read-through to Fastenal's own price-cost commentary for Q4. If it were priced, the downside skew would be steeper than +4.1.
findings.independence: Proxy only. The Q2 call said the price-cost gap would not close in 2H (https://www.webull.com/news/15267023071093760), a document shared with finding 3.

searched_and_found_nothing: A post-August refreshed consensus for Q3 revenue and EPS: Benzinga (403), TipRanks (MX listing only) and Seeking Alpha were paywalled or stale
MSC Industrial fiscal Q4 2026 results: not out until 2026-10-22, after the window
Grainger or other distributor September 2026 trend commentary: none found
Analyst preview notes or rating changes in September and October 2026: none found beyond the Baird target of $54 on 2026-08-07
Any Fastenal fall 2026 price-increase announcement: none found
CEO transition: a planned handover to Jeff Watts effective 2026-07-16, announced 2025-12-22 and fully public, so no finding

rejected_candidates.candidate: Planned CEO handover from Florness to Watts on 2026-07-16; this is the first print under the new CEO
rejected_candidates.detail: Announced in December 2025 and already covered at the Q2 print. It carries no sourced fact that bears on this print beyond what moves abs_move_pct up slightly.

baseline_tension: The findings net to about zero. The gross-margin negative agrees with the +4.1 put skew; the sales and SG&A-leverage positives cut against it but are mostly public. The stock near its 52-week high after a 3% 20-day run-up, with the last three prints sold, tilts the reaction slightly negative even if EPS beats by a cent.
lessons_applied: Rule 6, disputed bar: the EPS bar is $0.33 vs $0.34 and the revenue bar has one stale source. Revenue finding cut 0.4 -> 0.2 and SG&A/EPS finding 0.7 -> 0.4 (caps applied once, combined with rule 1 because this name sells its beats). p_up 46 -> 47.
Rule 6, inside guidance: the GM decline is largely inside management's seasonal guide and its statement that price-cost will not close. GM finding -1.0 -> -0.7.
Rule 2, one-off: the IEEPA refund has limited exposure and no path to the guide. 0.2 -> 0.1.
Rule 5, proxy: the ISM-prices read-through is unconfirmed by the company. -0.3 -> -0.2.
Rule 7: short interest checked (3.0% of float, 4.6 days to cover), not crowded, so the negatives were not shrunk for squeeze risk. abs_move_pct left at 4.8.
